sections.history: Thiruneeragam is not a temple of its own but a Divya Desam housed within the Ulagalantha Perumal Temple of Periya Kanchi, the same complex that holds Thiruooragam, Thirukkaragam and Thirukkarvanam. The four are believed to have once been independent shrines, brought together in this complex, and a single verse of Thirumangai Alvar names them all. Of the shrine itself, the Alvar's hymn is the firm testimony; one pasuram is credited to it in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. The host temple is believed to be a Pallava foundation, enlarged by the Cholas, the Vijayanagara kings and the Nayaks, and administered today by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE Department. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams of Thondai Nadu.
sections.architecture: The shrine sits within the walls of the Ulagalantha Perumal complex, with its own sanctum under the Jagadeeshwara Vimanam. Its sacred water is the Akrura Theertham. There is no fixed moolavar image here; it is the utsavar, the processional image, that is worshipped as Jagadeeshwara Perumal, with Nilamangaivalli Thayar as his consort. The Akrura of the Puranas is named as the devotee who beheld the Lord here.
sections.legends: The name Thiruneeragam carries the word neer, water, and devotional readers take it as a picture of the Lord himself: like water, giving itself equally to every being that comes to it. The sthala purana names Akrura, the devotee of Krishna, as the one who saw the Lord at this place, and the tank still bears his name. With Thiruooragam, Thirukkaragam and Thirukkarvanam it forms the four Divya Desams that tradition keeps within the one complex.
sections.festivals: Thiruneeragam shares the calendar of the Ulagalantha Perumal Temple: Vaikunta Ekadashi, the annual Brahmotsavam and the recitation of the Divya Prabandham in the month of Margazhi. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: A small and easily missed sanctum, best visited as part of the whole circuit of the complex. Seek it out after Thiruooragam, and ask the priests to show the Akrura Theertham and the utsavar of Jagadeeshwara Perumal. Pause here with the Alvar's single verse in mind; it is a place for quiet, not spectacle.

visit.timings: The shrine opens with the Ulagalantha Perumal Temple: morning and evening darshan sessions with a midday closure. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctums; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: This is a shrine inside the Ulagalantha Perumal Temple in the old town of Kanchipuram (Periya Kanchi); enter by that temple's gateway and ask for Thiruneeragam. Chennai, about 70 km to the north-east, is the nearest major airport, and Kanchipuram town is the nearest railhead.
